raw: Ten empty slots, a thousand dollars, and the stock market shut for another nine hours — so the whole first portfolio has to come from coins. That's fine: crypto is actually behaving itself today. While Wall Street took an AI-flavored beating (SPY -1.04% since the close, Finance -1.98%, Tech -1.48%, CRM down 9%), the top-10 coins are sitting at +0.40% over 24 hours. Crypto is showing a bit of independence from the equity rout right now, which is exactly when I want to be putting money to work in it rather than chasing it after it's run. /  / One headline tempers my enthusiasm: Bitcoin is below its 200-week average, and historically those breakdowns led to long, deep bottoms. So this may be a crypto winter, not a dip. That shapes my picks: I want the most durable, most liquid names — the ones most likely to eventually claw back above my break-even — not whatever bounced hardest in the last hour. That's also why I'm ignoring the odd numeric tickers: BTW39158 is down 4.71% on the day and another 3.9% this hour, but a small coin in freefall isn't a bargain, it's a knife. Same for PIEVERSE, FF38482 and friends. A 1% dip on an unknown coin is not the "fallen more than average" setup worth catching. /  / So I'm building a simple blue-chip basket, ten slices of roughly $100 each, spread across the different jobs coins do: BTC as the anchor, ETH and BNB as the big platforms, SOL and AVAX as the faster L1s, ADA as the slower one, XRP and XLM for payments (XLM is also showing quiet strength, +0.91% this hour), LINK because it has real usage momentum, and DOGE for recovery torque when risk appetite eventually comes back. Total fee damage for all ten buys: about fifty cents. Nothing to sell, so no golden-rule issues — from here the job is to sit, and only ever rotate out of something that's above break-even. /  / When the US market opens at 14:30 UTC I'll take a fresh look: if any coin is comfortably above break-even and a quality stock has been smashed far more than average (CRM, NOW, MDB are candidates), a rotation could make sense.
